newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner to step up Kleinwort integration.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner to step up Kleinwort integration.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said it would step up the integration of its British investment bank Kleinwort Benson in 1997, moving responsibility for the group's entire corporate finance and equity business to London.

It also plans to put the group's worldwide business in bonds, derivatives and foreign exchange under control from Frankfurt, management board member Hansgeorg Hofmann told reporters. The changes take effect at the start of 1997.
"In early 1997 will take forward the integration in a fairly visible way," Hofmann, who is responsible for investment banking, said. "We want to steer certain global business lines globally."
The reorganisation is likely to involve the movement of some staff between London and Frankfurt but details have not been decided yet, a spokesman said.

Dresdner's one-billion pound purchase of Kleinwort last year, its biggest single investment ever, was part of a drive by Germany's major banks to expand their investment banking and acquire foreign knowhow.
It followed Deutsche's decision in 1994 to concentrate its investment bank business at London subsidiary Morgan Grenfell.

Hofmann said Dresdner has taken a "softly, softly" approach in integrating Kleinwort with the aim of melding the culture of the financially strong universal bank with Kleinwort's expertise built up over its 200-year history.
"We didn't want to use our Teutonic boots at Kleinwort Benson, we wanted to give people time to feel comfortable and get used to each other," Hofmann said.

The bank also wants the group's various syndicated loans and project finance units worldwide to report to one person, Hofmann said, adding that it had not yet been decided where that person would be based.
In addition, Dresdner plans to build up a cross-border mergers and acquisitions business in Germany with Kleinwort's help.
"We are well-positioned in England but must build up a presence in Germany which Dresdner could never have done on its own, that's a challenge for the coming years," Hofmann said.
Hofmann said Dresdner would hire new staff wherever it saw gaps but indicated that Dresdner did not plan to embark on large hiring drives.
"We want to create a new culture, you can't do that by hiring 100 people, you can't create loyalty through cash," Hofmann said.
Rival Deutsche Bank AG has launched a recruitment drive and has been accused by rivals of poaching staff with "telephone number" pay packages, a charge it has denied.
Hofmann said Dresdner would have to expand its proprietary equity trading team, especially in London but also in Frankfurt.
